articleTitle: Hybrid optical receivers with integrated electronics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: 10 Gbit/s transimpedance optical receiver front-ends (RFEs) have been implemented with state-of-the-art high speed silicon bipolar and GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) technologies. RFEs with bandwidths between 8 to 10 GHz and sensitivity of around -22 dBm were predicted. Preliminary measurements of the RFEs using the GaAs HBT pre-amplifier design showed -3 dB bandwidths of 9.5-10 GHz and transimpedance of 310-340 Omega . Group delay variations of less than 30 ps have been achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Predicted signal-noise ratio of a P-I-N photodiode distributed amplifier combination
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The distributed amplifier photodiode combination shows a superior signal to noise ratio over the grounded source one when used with a lossy photodiode. A 8.34 dB improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio is predicted at a 40 GHz bandwidth. The effect of photodiode resistance on the signal to noise performance is very small.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 12 GHz PIN-HEMT optical receiver front end
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: An optical receiver has been designed and fabricated which has a transimpedance of 53 dB Omega , a bandwidth of 12.5 GHz and an equivalent input noise current of less than 11 pA/ square root Hz over the bandwidth. A sensitivity of -20.7 dBm has been measured at 10 Gbit/s using a 2/sup 7/-1 pattern. To the authors knowledge, this is the best measured sensitivity reported for a 10 Gbit/s receiver to date. Simulation shows that this receiver is capable of operation at 15 Gbit/s.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated 4.8 Gbit/s current-mode transimpedance optical preamplifier
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors describe an integrated wide-bandwidth, DC-coupled, current-mode preamplifier for photo-receiver applications. Common-gate configurations allow improved bandwidth and reduced sensitivity to detector capacitance variations compared with conventional common-source configurations. IC designs with projected speeds approaching 5 Gbit/s have been fabricated, the results will be used to design high-performance receivers targeted at 9.6 Gbit/s operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realization of fast photoreceivers based on ITO/n-GaAs Schottky diodes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: Excellent test ITO/n-GaAs Schottky diodes (ideality factor=1.07) have been fabricated by RF sputtering and this process has been optimised to produce high transmission (>90%), low resistivity (<2*10/sup -5/ Omega cm) and low leakage (<3 nA), responsivity=0.4A/W. These devices are designed to be monolithically integrated with HBTs to form fast photoreceivers for operation in the 800 nm wavelength for local communication networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: For ultraviolet radiation the use of silicon photodiodes is limited to specific measured wavelengths because of the difficulties involved with interpolation in that spectral region. The authors assess the feasibility of modelling the behaviour of silicon photodiodes sufficiently well to enable accurate interpolation and to associate uncertainties to the use of models describing the operation of silicon photodiodes in the ultraviolet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel optical receiver design using distributed amplifier pulse shaping network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: A novel method for operating the distributed amplifier as a transversal filter with gain at microwave frequencies has been presented and discussed. Simulation results show the practicability of the technique and its particular usefulness in optical systems where pulse shaping is required. The technique described is versatile since a range of receiver responses can be constructed by varying the FET gains and the effective stage delays. The ability to produce a well controlled receiver response makes this technique particularly useful for obtaining very wideband operation from available frequency-limited semiconductor processes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Avalanche multiplication and breakdown in GaAs/AlGaAs MQW in structures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors studied the effect of MQW dimensions on the ionisation coefficients of a series of MQW pin diodes structures for a wide range of well and barrier size. Breakdown voltage was measured and avalanche multiplication was found to be responsible for the breakdown observed. An analysis is presented for the results obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Post-detection chromatic dispersion equalisation using GaAs MMICs in heterodyne detection systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors have devised, fabricated and demonstrated the effectiveness of a GaAs MMIC fibre chromatic dispersion equaliser for application in heterodyne optical fibre systems. The results of the fabricated equaliser are found to be in good agreement with the analytic predictions, affording significant reductions in dispersion penalty of the detected signal at a bit rate of 5 Gbit/s. An important feature of this approach is that the use of GaAs MMIC technology allows dispersion compensation to be integrated with other receiver electronics, providing a practical and convenient solution to fibre group delay equalisation in heterodyne optical systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Erbium-doped fibre pre-amplifier with an integral band-pass filter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors have shown that significant optical gain improvements can be achieved by inserting a narrow band-pass filter within the erbium-doped fibre amplifiers length to suppress the built-up of both forward and backward ASE powers, accompanied by a noise figure reduction of 0.6-0.8 dB. The optimum filter position is found to be around 48% and 42% from the input end of the total amplifier length for 1.48 mu m and 0.98 mu m pump wavelengths respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x//Si multiquantum well IR detectors grown by low pressure vapour phase epitaxy
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors report measurements on Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x//Si MQW IR detectors grown by low-pressure vapour phase epitaxy (LP-VPE). Device characteristics such as the temperature-dependent IV curves, IR photoresponse and photoconductive gain are presented. It has been shown that the tunnelling component of the low temperature dark current in Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x//Si MQWs is very sensitive to B doping level in QWs for sample growth at 640 degrees C, low silane flow, and with doping across the full width of the QWs. For samples lightly doped in only the central 2/3 of each QW and grown at 610 degrees C and higher silane flow, low tunnelling currents were obtained. A photoresponse has been measured for the lightly doped structures in the 5-14 mu m range. A small peak at 11.5 mu m with a sharp cut-off at increasing wavelength is probably due to a QW transition because of its close agreement with E/sub a/ for the sample. The photoconductive gain derived from noise measurements shows no bias dependence for biases up to 0.1 V per period for both the 10 and 50 MQW period devices, suggesting that the hole mean free path remains constant. The gain shows the expected variation with the number of QWs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer modelling of the InGaAs HFETPD
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: A 2-D device simulation package has been developed which can be used to examine optoelectronic devices ranging from simple PIN Diodes to more recent structures such as the heterojunction field effect transistor photodetector (HFETPD). The HFETPD promises very low noise with avalanche gain and can be practically realised using indium based III-V semiconductors. The main part of the work so far has been centered around the modification and use of the 2-D device simulation package, these modifications have involved the inclusion of various models which describe some of the physics of indium based III-V semiconductors. A recent update has allowed the inclusion of an impact ionisation model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for the optical receiver performance analysis involving input optical amplifier noise
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Detectors and Receivers
abstract: The authors have described in detail a new approach for the analysis of optical preamplifier receiver performance. Through a rigorous statistical derivation, they have obtained formulas for the numerical calculation of the mean and variance of the receiver signal. Simulation has been carried out on a reported receiver system and results were compared with both the experimental data and those from other more established BER calculation methods. The discrepancies between the simulation results are discussed. It is concluded that this new approach is best suited for the preamplifier receiver performance analysis involving narrow bandpass optical filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
